en.name: Shaobing (sesame flatbread)
en.summary: A plain baked shaobing keeps 1–2 days loosely wrapped at room temperature, and 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F). It is an unpackaged, same-day bakery item with no preservatives, and the crisp layers are the first thing to go.
en.pantry: 1–2 days loosely wrapped at room temperature, and honestly it is a breakfast-morning food. The flaky layers go leathery within a day as moisture moves out of them, and the sesame on top slowly loses its toasted smell. Reheat dry in a pan rather than in a microwave — the pan drives moisture back out and the layers separate again, while the microwave steams them into something chewy. Do not seal a warm shaobing in a plastic bag; it makes its own steam and the crust is gone within the hour.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for shaobing, and the fridge is not a good home for it: cold makes the layers stale faster, because starch retrogradation runs quickest just above freezing. The one exception is a filled shaobing — split and stuffed with egg, beef, pork floss or youtiao. That is a made-up meal rather than a bread, and it belongs at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and should be eaten the same day, because the filling sets the timeline, not the pastry.
en.freezer: 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F), and freeze it plain and unfilled. Cool it completely, bag it with the air pressed out, and reheat from frozen in a hot oven or an air fryer until the layers crisp again. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well past a month — the window describes drying and freezer burn rather than safety — and the figure here is a conservative quality estimate rather than a published number.
en.thawing: Reheat from frozen in a hot oven or air fryer. Do not thaw first, and never thaw a filled one on the counter; a filled shaobing thaws in the fridge.
spoilage: Layers gone soft and leathery, no longer separating when reheated.
A rancid or stale smell from the sesame and the fat in the layers.
Mould spots, which come quickly on a bread sealed while warm.
A sour smell from a filled shaobing, which means the filling has gone.
tips: Reheat dry in a pan or an oven, never in the microwave.
Freeze them plain; fill them after reheating.
Let them cool completely before bagging so they do not steam themselves.
Buy them in the morning and eat them in the morning — that is what the food is.

faq.a: 1–2 days loosely wrapped at room temperature. The figure is read across from doughnuts; nobody publishes one for shaobing.
Yes, 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F), plain and unfilled. Reheat from frozen in a hot oven or an air fryer.

faq.q: How do you reheat shaobing so it is crisp again?
faq.a: Dry heat — a pan, an oven or an air fryer. A microwave steams the layers and turns them chewy.

zh.name: 燒餅
zh.summary: 原味燒餅鬆鬆包好放室溫可放 1～2 天，−18 °C 冷凍是 1 個月。它是沒有包裝、沒有防腐劑、當天現做的烘焙品，最先失去的就是那層酥。
zh.pantry: 鬆鬆包好、室溫 1～2 天，但老實說它就是早餐那個早上的食物。層次會在一天內因為水分往外跑而變得韌韌的，表面的芝麻也會慢慢失去焙香。回熱請用乾鍋，不要微波——乾鍋把水分逼出去，層次會重新分開；微波則是把它蒸成一塊會黏牙的東西。還熱著的燒餅千萬不要密封進塑膠袋，它會自己悶出蒸氣，一小時內酥皮就沒了。
zh.fridge: 燒餅沒有公布的冷藏期限，而冷藏也不是它的好去處：低溫會讓層次更快老化，因為澱粉回凝在略高於冰點時跑得最快。唯一的例外是夾了餡的燒餅——夾蛋、夾牛肉、夾肉鬆或夾油條。那已經是一份現做的餐點而不是麵包，該放 4 °C 以下，而且當天吃完，因為決定期限的是餡料而不是餅皮。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 1 個月，而且要冷凍原味、不夾餡的。完全放涼、壓出空氣裝袋，要吃時直接從冷凍進高溫烤箱或氣炸鍋，烤到層次重新酥起來。只要全程沒退冰，放超過一個月仍然安全——這個期限講的是變乾和凍燒，不是安全——而且這個數字是保守的品質估計，不是公布的數據。
zh.thawing: 直接從冷凍進高溫烤箱或氣炸鍋回烤，不要先解凍。夾餡的那種絕對不要放在檯面上解凍，要放冷藏。
spoilage: 層次變軟變韌，回烤也分不開了。
芝麻和層次裡的油脂聞起來油耗或走味。
長霉——還熱著就密封的餅特別快。
夾餡燒餅聞起來發酸，那表示餡料壞了。
tips: 回熱用乾鍋或烤箱，絕對不要微波。
冷凍要冷凍原味的；回烤之後再夾餡。
完全放涼再裝袋，免得它自己把自己蒸軟。
早上買、早上吃——這種食物本來就是這樣的。

faq.a: 鬆鬆包好放室溫 1～2 天。這個數字是比照甜甜圈而來，沒有人為燒餅公布過期限。
可以，−18 °C 下 1 個月，要冷凍原味不夾餡的。要吃時直接從冷凍進高溫烤箱或氣炸鍋。
用乾熱——平底鍋、烤箱或氣炸鍋。微波會把層次蒸軟，變得黏牙。
